newsitem.title: UK: CARIPLO sets 3-tranche 5-year euro-fungible bond. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CARIPLO sets 3-tranche 5-year euro-fungible bond. [CORRECTED 14:50 GMT]

text.p: Cassa di Risparmio delle Provincie Lombarde has issued a three-tranche five-year deal, in French francs, lire and marks, which will be redenominated into euros after EMU and then be fungible, CARIPLO and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said as joint lead managers on Monday.
J.P. Morgan is joint lead on the lira transaction while DMG is senior co-lead manager.
There is a 1.0 billion franc bond, a 600 billion lire bond and a 300 million mark bond.

The French franc and mark bonds carry a coupon of three-month LIBOR plus 10 b.p.. The lira bond pays 6.25 percent initially but, at CARIPLO's option, the option may be changed to three-month LIBOR plus 10 b.p. on any coupon date.
(Corrects to make clear that French franc and mark bonds carry a coupon of three-month LIBOR plus 10 basis points and not 6.25 percent.)
TYPE FRN MARGIN +10 BP PAY DATE 18.AUG.97
TYPE FRN MARGIN +10 BP PAY DATE 08.AUG.97
ON ANY COUPON DATE AT BORROWERS OPTION.
